New Web Tool Maps Fossil Locations Across Ancient Continents in Seconds

2026-07-20 University of Barcelona / Phys.org paleogeography, PACA, paleocoordinates, plate tectonics, fossil mapping, University of Barcelona, GPlates, Scientific Reports, open science, paleontology
Read the source article

Quick summary

The University of Barcelona's BIOST3 Research Group has developed PACA, an open-access web tool that transforms current geographic coordinates into paleocoordinates across geological time, making high-quality paleogeographic reconstructions accessible to researchers and the public without programming skills.

Key takeaways

  • PACA (Paleocoordinates Calculator) is an open-access web interface that simplifies the process of determining fossil locations throughout geological history
  • Users simply upload a CSV file with current coordinates and geological age to obtain exact paleocoordinates in seconds, removing the programming barrier of traditional tectonic reconstruction software
  • The tool's mathematical core is based on the R package palaeoverse, connecting directly to the GPlates web service for plate tectonics reconstructions
  • PACA supports comparison with up to five global plate models widely used by the scientific community: PALEOMAP, GOLONKA, MERDITH2021, TorsvikCocks2017, and MATTHEWS
  • Both the PACA source code and 3D conversion scripts are publicly available on the Zenodo repository, following open science principles of transparency and reproducibility
